output:
To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Embakasi Monday 30 Nov — casuals pay, what you can promise, and the Kisumu loading (draft for Brian)

EMBAKASI, MONDAY 30 NOVEMBER — BRIEFING NOTE FOR BRIAN OCHIENG
From Achieng Otieno (HR). Draft, written Saturday night. Read it once tonight, once in the car.

Brian,

Everything here is checked against the bank's rejection notice, Kevin's note, NW's approval yesterday morning, Peninah's update and Joseph's report this evening. It's written so you can use it standing up.

1. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED ON FRIDAY
- Payroll sent the fortnightly casual payment as a bulk bank file — 212 people, file TLL-CAS-2611B.
- The bank rejected the entire file at validation at 13:52 on Friday. One column, the beneficiary reference, was over the 20-character limit the bank introduced with its 25 November platform upgrade. Nothing in that file was processed. Not one person was paid.
- The rejection alert went to the old finance mailbox. Kevin only saw it after 5pm, and by then the bank's cut-off had passed, so the file couldn't be fixed and re-sent the same day.
- That's the whole story, and it's ours: our file, our old template, our mailbox. The men's details were fine. Nobody at the depot did anything wrong, and I don't want anyone thinking this is about them.

2. WHERE THE MONEY IS NOW
- NW approved the M-Pesa B2C route on Saturday morning at 09:15. That's the route we're on.
- Peninah has been through the list: 198 numbers confirmed, 14 she couldn't reach, mostly the new loaders from the Athi River intake.
- Kevin's realistic landing time is Monday by 11am. He was clear he won't promise earlier, and neither should you.
- Also approved, in the same batch, paid by the company and not deducted from anyone: KES 500 per head for Monday lunch and fare, for every casual on the affected list.
- M-Pesa charges are on us.
- Peninah will be at Embakasi from 7:30 with a printout, so the 14 can give her correct numbers face to face. She's carrying the laptop and will print payslips for anyone who wants one.

3. WHAT YOU CAN PROMISE — SAY IT PLAINLY
- "You will be paid on Monday, by 11am, on M-Pesa."
- "The KES 500 for lunch and fare comes in the same payment."
- "The M-Pesa charges are ours. Nothing is deducted from you."
- "If your rent is due on the 1st, the money is in your phone before then."
- "Peninah is here from 7:30. If your number has changed, or you're not sure it's right, go to her and she'll fix it and print your payslip."
- "Management got this wrong, and I'm apologising to you in person. That's why I'm standing here."

For the 14, only this: "Peninah will take your correct number today. Once it's captured, yours goes in the next batch." Don't put a time on that one. We don't control it yet.

4. WHAT YOU MUST NOT PROMISE
- Nothing earlier than 11am. Not "first thing", not "by lunch", not "before ten". In 2024 in Mombasa a supervisor told the casuals "by lunch"; the money came at 4pm and half the shift sat down. We never again give a time we can't keep. 11am is the only time in your mouth.
- No cash, and no "I'll follow up personally and push it through". You can't speed it up, and saying so makes you the man who owes them.
- Nothing about contracts. No permanence, no "we'll look after you after this", and no "we'll remember who loaded and who didn't". The procedure forbids dismissal threats on the day; that includes the soft version. Not a word about contracts on Monday.
- No speculation about why. Don't blame the bank, don't blame finance, don't blame Nairobi. "We got it wrong, and here's when the money lands" is enough. This is our mess, not theirs, and you shouldn't go in defensive.
- Nothing about the company's finances, in any form. If someone asks whether the company is short, the answer is: "The payment is approved and it lands by 11am. That's what I'm here to tell you." Then move on.

5. MONDAY MORNING, IN ORDER
- 05:30, you're at the depot. Walk the yard, greet the early ones, don't open with a speech.
- Before the shift meeting, get Ouma on his own. Privately. He's loud but he's not a bad man — four kids, rent due on the 1st, and he has heard "tomorrow" before. Say something like: "Ouma, I'm not here to argue. You weren't paid on Friday because our payment file was rejected and we saw it too late. That's on us. The money comes Monday by 11am on M-Pesa, plus 500 for lunch and fare, charges on us. I'm sorry. I'd rather hear from you what the men are saying than have you hear it from me through a crowd." Then listen. Don't correct him in front of anyone.
- Then the whole group, short: what happened, 11am, the 500, Peninah at 7:30, the apology. Five minutes, not fifteen. Take questions, but only answer what you actually know.
- The apology is yours to make, from management, as NW asked. Not Joseph's, not Peninah's.

6. IF OUMA'S GROUP WON'T LOAD THE KISUMU TRUCKS
- The 9am departure is the constraint: miss it and we miss the mill's offloading slot. Treat 9am as your decision point, not as the deadline for winning the argument.
- A stoppage is not a grievance channel. Under the casuals procedure, any stoppage is handled by Operations and HR together — you and me, not the supervisors alone and not you improvising.
- So: no shouting, no threats, no bringing in outside labour to load, and not a word about contracts or dismissal. The procedure says no one is dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day. That isn't a technicality — it's what stops this becoming a fight.
- The order I'd follow: shift starts at 06:00, ask them to load as normal while the pay runs. If they refuse, ask for ten minutes with Ouma and two of the others, away from the trucks, and ask one question: "What do you need to see to load?" If it's proof, Peninah can show them the batch — their names, their amounts, the 11am. That's evidence, not a new promise.
- If they still refuse, don't force it and don't stand there arguing. Tell them straight: "The trucks leave at 9. If they don't load, that's a lost consignment, and it doesn't change your pay — you're still paid by 11am." Then hand the trucks to Operations: tell transport and the mill the 9am slot is at risk, and see whether a partial load with whoever is willing gets it out. Don't push individuals to break ranks in front of the group — that turns a pay dispute into a fight among the men.
- Then call me. I'm up from 4:30. WhatsApp me before 7:05 if anything has moved, because after that I'm in the air to Entebbe and I land around 8:45. Between 7:05 and 8:45 this note is your authority: talk first, no threats, protect the pay promise, and let the consignment be the thing that suffers, not the men.
- Log it as it happens — times, who you spoke to, what was said. Not to use against anyone. We need it for the joint Ops/HR report and to back up Joseph's account.

7. SMALL THINGS
- Don't read this out. It's for you.
- Don't say "I know how you feel."
- Don't let Joseph or anyone else make promises on your behalf.
- Don't take the anger personally. It isn't about you, and after six years they know that.

I'll read this before I sleep and message you if I change anything. Otherwise: 11am, the 500, Peninah at 7:30, Ouma first and privately, no contracts, no threats — and call me when you can.

Achieng

reasons: The note says NW approved the plan yesterday morning, but the approval was given that same Saturday morning.
